brief.headline: Secure supply first, then recover ₹3.37 L/yr by moving to the price we already pay elsewhere — they are loss-making and in the distress zone, so qualify a second source now.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹1.62/NOS on the LDPE bottle (our best price today), closing a 4.3% gap.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS for LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE, saving ₹3.37 L/yr
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited ₹1.62/NOS for the same item; Berry charges ₹1.69/NOS. The market typical for similar caps is ₹0.85–0.95/pc and fair, so ₹1.62 is a reasonable benchmark. Berry is a trader (100.0% traded revenue), so their price carries a reseller margin — push toward the maker's price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 Days After Receipt — do not extend further, because they are already loss-making and cash-tight.

brief.financialLeverage: Berry lost money in FY2023-24 (profit kept: -199.2%, vs 2.3% for similar firms) and sits in the distress zone (Altman Z: -0.18, health score: 0/100). They owe 220.44x their own cash and their cash is stuck for 335d (vs 70d for peers). Despite that fragility, we are a big customer — our ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr in sales — so they need us. Lead with supply security and qualifying a second source, not a hard price squeeze that could tip them over, but use our 7.21% share to anchor the ask at the ₹1.62/NOS price we already pay.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health 65/100) with pharma bottles and caps — the strongest second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, profitable rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health 73/100) covering bottles and closures — a robust alternate.

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already our best-price supplier at ₹1.62/NOS for the same LDPE bottle — expand volume with them to reduce dependence on Berry.

risks: Berry is loss-making and in the distress zone — pushing too hard on price could break supply; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek now.
They owe 220.44x their own cash and have very weak money-health (1/10) — a supply-continuity risk if cash runs out.
As a pure trader (100.0% traded), they have no direct cost anchor and may resist matching a maker's price — be ready to walk to Manjushree.
Our ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their sales, so losing us hurts them — but their desperation may also mean they cannot sustain the discount long-term.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but we need to talk about price and supply security — we're paying ₹1.69 here when we already pay ₹1.62 elsewhere, and we want to make sure you're stable enough to keep delivering.
